pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Mission and Values | Norwood Primary & Pre-School
pageCache.text:
Vision, Mission and Values
Our Vision:
An inclusive community where every child feels safe, valued, and inspired to flourish with confidence and compassion.
Our Mission:
For all our children to feel safe, secure and mentally healthy so that they can flourish.
To have the highest aspirations and ambitions for our children, both academically and personally.
Celebrate our differences and build a strong, caring community where every voice is valued and every child belongs, no matter their race, religion, culture, background or disability.
To foster resilience, self-belief and a life-long love of learning so that our children are ready for the challenges and successes of life.

It is a pleasure to welcome you to Norwood Primary and Pre-School.
Welcome to Norwood Primary and Pre-School – a happy, inclusive, and inspiring school in the heart of Eastleigh Town Centre where every child is valued.
Our incredible staff team and governors have high aspirations and expectations for each child and endeavour to help every one of them to flourish and reach their full potential. We pride ourselves on our nurturing approach and our special family feel is evident as you walk around our school.
We believe that childhood should be joyful. Our school values of Aspiration, Belonging and Compassion flow through everything we do and everything we believe in. From the classroom to the playground, we encourage children to take pride in their learning, respect one another, build a strong sense of belonging within the school community and grow into resilient, compassionate learners ready for the future.
Whether you are a current member of our school community or considering Norwood for your child, we hope our website gives you a flavour of life at our school. Please do not hesitate to get in touch if you would like to visit us or have any questions—we would be delighted to welcome you in person.
Thank you for visiting and we look forward to sharing our journey with you.

Breakfast Club
Norwood Primary School Breakfast Club provides childcare for parents between 7.45 am and 8.30 am. Monday to Friday, term time only. We do not operate Breakfast Club on School Closure days.
Breakfast Club is located in the Nutbeem Hall. Entry is via the main Nutbeem door and is manned until 8.00 am. After 8.00 am, the children need to be brought to the School Office for entry to Breakfast Club. Children need to arrive no later than 8.15 am if they wish to have breakfast.
The session rate is £5.00. Breakfast includes:
• Cereals and/or toast (with various toppings)
Educational games and activities will be provided for the children attending Breakfast Club after they have finished their breakfast. We aim to promote and develop positive personal and social skills associated with eating together e.g. manners, passing cutlery or toppings, conversation skills, turn taking and sharing. In addition, we encourage the children to develop healthy habits, including washing hands before eating.
The Breakfast Club is fully inclusive and open to all children who attend Norwood Primary School. We promote equal opportunities in line with Norwood Primary School’s policy. We will take all reasonable steps to enable any children with disabilities to attend.

Personal Development
At Norwood Primary & Pre-School, personal development is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our values of Aspiration, Belonging and Compassion, we are committed to helping every child flourish academically, socially and emotionally in a happy, inclusive and nurturing environment.
We use the PSHE Association programme to support the planning and development of our PSHE education, citizenship curriculum, and aspects of our provision that contribute to the Enrichment Benchmark criteria, such as promoting children's personal development, character, leadership, and active participation in school and community life.
The People Project is our whole-school curriculum thread that introduces children to a diverse range of significant people from different backgrounds, cultures, careers and periods in history. Through exploring their lives, achievements and values, pupils develop their understanding of the world, build aspirations for their own futures, and deepen their learning across PSHE, citizenship, British Values, SMSC, and the wider curriculum.
The People Project
The People Project is a personal development curriculum designed to nurture the whole child, equipping them with the knowledge, skills, and character traits they need to thrive in an ever-changing world. Rooted in our values of Aspiration, Belonging, and Compassion, this curriculum empowers children to dream big, feel connected, and act with kindness—both within their school community and beyond.
For all our children to feel safe, secure and mentally healthy so that they can flourish.
To have the highest aspirations and ambitions for our children, both academically and personally.
Celebrate our differences and build a strong, caring community where every voice is valued and every child belongs, no matter their race, religion, culture, background or disability.
To foster resilience, self-belief and a life-long love of learning so that our children are ready for the challenges and successes of life.
The People Project responds to this by creating meaningful opportunities for pupils to explore who they are, how they relate to others, and how they can contribute positively to society.
By weaving these values into every aspect of learning, The People Project is more than a curriculum—it is a commitment to shaping confident, compassionate individuals who aspire to make a difference.
The idea behind this project is:
to inspire children through an array of individuals in a variety of subjects
to teach children equity, equality, diversity, inclusion, respect and acceptance
to give children aspirations and a map of how to achieve their goals
to improve the amount of teaching surrounding the protected characteristics
Each term is based on one of our school values.
start with an assembly introducing the value, the person and how they link.

have an outcome for each class to contribute into a floor book.

We offer a range of leadership opportunities for children to develop their confidence, responsibility and sense of belonging and citizenship within the school community. These include:
School Voices (Pupil Researchers)- with the University of Southampton
Food Focus Group- working with Edwards and Ward, our school caterers
A very warm welcome to Norwood Pre-School

Governing Body
On behalf of the Governing Body, I welcome you to Norwood Primary and Pre school.
Our Headteacher and staff work tirelessly to make sure that every child is seen and valued as an individual and that they each have the best possible start to their education. The Governors, Headteacher and all of the staff make every decision based on the best interests of the children, and I am very proud to be the Chair of the Governing body.
The Governing Body is committed to making a positive contribution to the school and education of our children. Our main role is to support, challenge and monitor what happens in the school by working in close partnership with the Headteacher and leadership team to help the school’s performance improve along with the future development of Norwood. The Governing body has an important role in shaping the future as well as wide-ranging statutory responsibilities.
All Governors are volunteers and each has a variety of experience. Each governor is appointed initially for a period of 4 years, and we have a good blend of governors in terms of their length of time with the school. The governing body has representation from Parents, staff, the local authority and the community. We meet as a whole team every half term with a strong focus on continuous improvement in teaching and learning,
Financial matters, decisions on spending priorities and school resourcing is the remit of the Finance and resources committee, that reports to the Governing Body.
In order for Governors to fulfil their roles, we make planned and unplanned visits to the school to talk to pupils and staff and to look at materials to make sure that things are being done in line with the agreed plan for the school. Governors attend training sessions and receive briefings from the school and Hampshire Services for Schools, as well as attending school events and activities.
All Governor meetings are minuted and are available at the school office – do ask if you would like to see them.
The Governing Body is determined to do our absolute best for the school. We value the contributions of everyone here who works so hard to ensure the children really are at the heart of the school.
We really would like to hear your views and suggestions, so please do not hesitate to contact me through our clerk.
With my very best wishes
Mrs Jane Stone - Chair
Mr Dan Kronbergs - Vice-Chair

pageCache.text:
Clubs & Activities
'Active for All' run our daily after school childcare club.
Their club provides care for children from the end of the school day up to 5.45pm. They offer a wide range of fun and engaging activities. If children would prefer to relax they can play with Lego or partake in arts and crafts. All Active for All staff are qualified and experienced in many different sports and activities so children will always have the best experience possible.
Session prices are as follows:
After school 3pm - 4.45pm - £8.50 per session
After school extended finish 4.45pm - 5.45pm - additional £3.50 per session
(important note: please check with Active For All for the most up to date prices)
Snack is included which will be a sandwich, yoghurt and fruit.
For more details or to book sessions please go to www.activeforall.co.uk
On collection at the main school office please use the door bell on the left hand side to alert Active for All of your arrival to collect. ​​​​​
After School Sports Clubs
Our engaging sessions are designed to empower participants to boost their confidence through the excitement of sports.
Led by qualified coaches with extensive experience in delivering P.E. sessions, our sessions foster both skill development and fun. Participants will not only learn the value of teamwork but will also be in an enjoyable environment, ultimately enhancing their social skills.
Sessions run Monday, Wednesday and Fridays after school from 3.15pm - 4.15pm. For more information and to book sessions please follow this link Let's Work Together – Building Communities or see the flyer below.
We run a range of teacher-led, free-of-charge clubs that take place after school or during lunchtimes, including:

General Information about Pre-School
We are open from 8.45am – 3pm term time only and will close on INSET days in line with the school.
At Norwood Primary pre-school we offer 3 different sessions in order to be as flexible as possible for our parents. The session times are as follows;
Morning Session – 8.45am until 11:45am
Afternoon Session – 12.30pm until 3pm
All Day Session – 8.45am until 3pm
The days available may vary depending on the amount of children in the setting.
Each family is assigned a keyworker from the pre-school staff team who will be responsible for getting to know your child and supporting him/her to settle and support his/her development whilst in pre-school. You are welcome to speak to any member of the staff team but we would recommend that you try to see your child’s keyworker in the first instance.
Uniform is not compulsory; the children need to wear comfortable clothes that they can move freely in and begin to manage independently. Aprons and overalls are provided but the children also need to be able to get messy! We use the outdoor area daily so appropriate clothing for the weather needs to be worn to pre-school. We ask that parents provide a change of clothes in a named bag each session in case of accidents and spills.
Positive attitudes to health and well-being are fostered through snack times during each session where the children are offered a range of nutritious snacks and fruit alongside milk and water. The fee payable for this is £1.00 per week payable through Arbor. A full term's snack fee will be added to Arbor at the start of each term for payment.
At lunch time the children eat with their friends and the staff team within the setting. They can bring a healthy lunch box from home or choose from a vegetarian or meat option menu which is freshly prepared in the school kitchen at a cost of £2.75 per day.
Lunches and Snacks can be paid using the Arbor App.
Children have easy access to the low level toilets within the setting at all times and accidents will be dealt with quickly and quietly in order to minimise distress for the child. Parents are asked to provide spare clothes in case of accidents/spills.
Whilst it is our expectation that your child will be toilet trained before starting in our setting we are aware that young children develop at different rates and some children may still need support to achieve independence. Young children are learning to manage their own physical and hygiene needs in a pre-school setting and the role of the adult is to support and encourage this independence. Please provide wipes and spare pull-ups or nappies if required. A Changing Log is maintained by staff.
In line with good practice and the school’s policy, please do not send your child to pre-school if they have been unwell with sickness, diarrhea or vomiting the night before or on the morning they are due to attend and for 48 hours after the last attack. Germs and viruses spread quickly between young children!
We encourage and support good hygiene and self-care with regular toilet and hand washing routines throughout the day.
If your child is unwell during a pre-school session we will contact you to collect him/her. Please ensure that all contact details are
Should you require your child to stay at preschool for longer than their funded hours entitlement, the hourly rate is £7.00. You will receive an invoice for any additional hours at the beginning of the month, for the month in advance
Should you have any further queries at all, please do not hesitate to call us on 02380 322 582 or email info@norwoodprimary.com

pageCache.text:
Pupil & Sports Premium
PE and Sports Premium
What is the Sports Premium?
The Sport Premium is allocated to schools in order to improve the provision of PE and School Sport, and ensure that pupils may lead healthier lifestyles.
What is the purpose of this funding?
Schools must spend the additional funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this.
Possible uses for the funding might include:
hiring specialist PE teachers or qualified sports coaches to work with primary teachers when teaching PE
supporting and engaging the least active children through new or additional clubs
paying for professional development opportunities for teachers in PE and sport
providing cover to release teachers for professional development in PE and sport
running sport competitions, or increasing pupils’ participation in the School Games
buying quality assured professional development modules or materials for PE and sport
providing places for pupils on after school sports clubs and holiday clubs
pooling the additional funding with that of other local schools.
For further information on the Sports Premium Funding click here:

School History
Percy Norwood - Our School Hero!
Norwood was opened in 1977 as a Primary School, its name taken from local hero Percy Norwood who was awarded the Edward Medal for Gallantry by King George V after saving a man’s life on the railway lines at Liss in 1913.
